mainTopic: Why a midwife touching a dead fetus in the womb is טמא, the source of the מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, and a new משנה on a fetus's foreleg that came out
overview: The גמרא asks why a midwife who touches a dead fetus inside the womb becomes טמא, when hidden things like two swallowed rings do not spread טומאה. רבה says a fetus is different because it will come out, but רבא rejects this, since a ring also comes out. רבא then brings רב יוסף's teaching in the name of שמואל: this טומאה is only a rabbinic decree, even according to רבי ישמעאל, who holds a fetus in the womb is טהור by Torah law. רב הושעיא explains the decree: maybe the baby put its head out and went back in without the midwife noticing. The mother is not included because she feels her own body, and she does not warn the midwife because she is too distracted by the pain of labor. The גמרא then shows where רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא get their views, and how each one uses the פסוקים ״על פני השדה״ and ״במת בנפש״ for different lessons, including the rules about a רביעית of blood. Finally, a new משנה begins about a fetus whose foreleg came out before its mother was slaughtered. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about the status of the flesh.

steps.title: The fetus and midwife look like the two-rings case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the עובר and the חיה are like the two rings, yet the משנה says the fetus makes the midwife טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the case of the fetus and the midwife. It is just like two rings, and yet the fetus makes the midwife impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge from the משנה's case of a midwife touching a dead fetus inside the womb. It seems to clash with the earlier rule about the two rings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rings case, something hidden inside a body does not pass טומאה to something else. The fetus is hidden inside the womb, and the midwife's hand is also inside, so we would expect no טומאה. Yet the משנה rules that the midwife is טמא.

phrases.english: But what about the fetus and the midwife,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's case: a dead fetus inside its mother, and a midwife who reached in and touched it.

phrases.english: which are like two rings,
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier case of two swallowed rings, where hidden impurity inside a body does not spread.

phrases.english: and yet the fetus makes the midwife impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עוּבָּר וְחַיָּה, דְּכִשְׁתֵּי טַבָּעוֹת דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge by comparing the משנה's midwife case to the earlier two-rings case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the חיה is טמא from touching a dead fetus in the womb.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hidden things inside a body (like two swallowed rings) do not pass טומאה to each other; the fetus and the midwife's hand are both hidden inside, so the midwife should stay טהור.

steps.title: רבה: a fetus is different because it will come out
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that a fetus is different from a ring because it will eventually leave the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: A fetus is different, since in the end it will come out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by pointing to a difference between a fetus and a ring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the fetus is destined to come out, it is not treated as truly hidden or swallowed. That is why, according to רבה, it can make the midwife טמא even while still inside.

phrases.english: Rabba said: A fetus is different,
since it will ultimately come out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: שָׁאנֵי עוּבָּר, הוֹאִיל וְסוֹפוֹ לָצֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fetus is hidden inside the body just like a swallowed ring, so it should not pass on טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A fetus is destined to leave the womb, so it is not treated like a swallowed item.

steps.title: רבא: a ring also comes out in the end
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רבה's answer: a swallowed ring will also come out eventually.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Are you saying a fetus will come out, but a ring will not come out?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רבה's answer with a question that is really a rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A swallowed ring will also be passed out of the body sooner or later. So 'it will eventually come out' does not separate the fetus from the ring, and רבה's distinction falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It will not eventually come out

steps.confusionAlert: This is phrased as a question, but רבא is not asking for information. He means: of course a ring also comes out! It is a rejection of רבה's answer.

phrases.english: Rava said: A fetus will ultimately come out,
and a ring will not ultimately come out?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: עוּבָּר סוֹפוֹ לָצֵאת, טַבַּעַת אֵין סוֹפָהּ לָצֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's answer from step 2.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A swallowed ring will also leave the body eventually, so 'it will come out' is not a real difference.

steps.title: רבא points to the scholars of פומבדיתא, meaning רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the scholars of פומבדיתא know the real reason, and identifies them as רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The people of פומבדיתא know the reason for this matter. And who is that? רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבה's answer, רבא sets up a new answer by pointing to רב יוסף. The actual answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that a new approach is replacing the rejected one. רבא does not give the reason himself yet; he tells us whose teaching holds the key.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new answer after a rejected one

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The people of Pumbedita know the reason for this matter,
and who is it? Rav Yosef.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: פּוּמְבְּדִיתָאֵי יָדְעִי טַעְמָא דְּהָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבה's answer, רבא introduces a new source for the answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setup for a new answer from another authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We need a reason why the fetus makes the midwife טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is found in the teaching of רב יוסף, quoted next.

steps.title: שמואל: this impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes שמואל: the midwife's טומאה is not from the Torah but from דברי סופרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: This impurity is not from the Torah, but from the words of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the real answer to the challenge: the midwife's טומאה is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the midwife's טומאה in the משנה does not come from the Torah but from a decree of the חכמים. So the משנה's ruling does not clash with the rule that hidden things do not spread טומאה. Steps 6-7 explain that this holds even for רבי ישמעאל, who says the fetus is טהור by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic law, the words of the Sages

steps.whyThisMatters: This resolves the whole challenge: the rule of hidden things not spreading טומאה stays true by Torah law, and the midwife case is a rabbinic addition.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: As Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This impurity is not from Torah law,
but rather from rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָה זוֹ אֵינָהּ מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אֶלָּא מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the answer that רבא attributed to רב יוסף in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the level of the law (rabbinic, not Torah)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ruling seemed to be Torah law, contradicting the rings case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The midwife's טומאה is only מדרבנן, so there is no contradiction with the Torah rule about hidden things.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טומאה of a midwife touching a dead fetus in the womb is from דברי סופרים, not Torah law.

steps.title: Why did שמואל say it both ways?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל meant by saying both 'not from the Torah' and 'but from the Sages.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it mean, 'not from Torah law but from rabbinic law'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל used this double wording. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It would have been enough to say 'it is rabbinic.' The extra words 'not from the Torah' seem to be pushing back against some opinion that it is Torah law.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'it is not from Torah law'
'but rather from rabbinic law'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵינָהּ מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of שמואל's statement in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why שמואל stressed that the טומאה is 'not from the Torah' instead of just saying it is rabbinic.

steps.title: Even רבי ישמעאל agrees there is a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: שמואל meant that the ruling is not only like רבי עקיבא; even רבי ישמעאל, who holds the fetus is טהור by Torah law, agrees the חכמים decreed טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that you should not say this follows only רבי עקיבא, who said a fetus in a woman's womb is impure. Rather, even according to רבי ישמעאל, who said a fetus in a woman's womb is pure, the Sages decreed impurity on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains שמואל's double wording: it shows that the משנה fits every opinion, not just רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that touching a dead fetus in the womb makes one טמא by Torah law, so the משנה would be easy for him. שמואל's wording teaches that even רבי ישמעאל, who says it is טהור by Torah law, agrees the חכמים added a rabbinic decree. So the משנה works for both.

keyTerms.meaning: So that you should not say

steps.whatToRemember: The midwife's טומאה in the משנה is a rabbinic decree that everyone agrees to, even רבי ישמעאל, who holds the fetus in the womb is טהור by Torah law.

phrases.english: So that you should not say it is according to Rabbi Akiva
who says: 'A fetus in a woman's womb is impure,'
phrases.notes: He means someone who touches the dead fetus there becomes טמא by Torah law.

phrases.english: rather, even according to Rabbi Yishmael
who says: 'A fetus in a woman's womb is pure,'
they decreed impurity on it by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא תֵּימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's wording shows the ruling is not only like רבי עקיבא (Torah-level טומאה); even רבי ישמעאל (Torah-level טהרה) agrees to a rabbinic decree of טומאה.

steps.title: Why did the Sages make this decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rabbinic decree of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the טומאה is a rabbinic decree, the גמרא asks why the חכמים made it. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If by Torah law the hidden fetus does not pass on טומאה, there must be a concern that led the חכמים to add this rule.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the rabbinic decree established in step 7 by asking its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the חכמים decreed טומאה on the midwife.

steps.title: רב הושעיא: maybe the baby put its head out
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא explains the decree: we worry the baby may have put its head out of the womb's opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: It is a decree, in case the baby put its head out past the opening of the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא gives the reason for the rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a baby's head comes out, it counts as born, and then touching it makes one טמא by Torah law. The חכמים worried this might have happened without the midwife noticing, so they made her טמא in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: The passage or opening of the womb

steps.whatToRemember: The midwife is טמא only מדרבנן, because of a concern that the baby's head may have come out unnoticed.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
It is a decree, lest the baby put out
its head outside the opening of the womb.
phrases.notes: Once the head comes out, the baby counts as born, so touching it would then make her טמא by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יוֹצִיא וָלָד רֹאשׁוֹ חוּץ לַפְּרוֹזְדוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree exists in case the baby put its head out of the womb's opening (making it born and Torah-level טמא) without the midwife noticing.

steps.title: Why not make the mother impure too?
steps.stepSummary: If the worry is that the baby's head came out without anyone noticing, the mother should also be made טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the woman should also be impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הושעיא's reason for the decree. If the baby's head may have come out unnoticed, why does the decree stop at the חיה and not include the mother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הושעיא said the חכמים decreed טומאה because the baby's head may have left the womb. The mother is in the same situation as the midwife, so the same worry seems to apply to her. The גמרא wants to know why the decree is limited.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge built on what was just said

phrases.english: If so, the woman too?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אִשָּׁה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 9 by applying it to the mother.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הושעיא's reason for the decree on the midwife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is that the head may have come out unnoticed, it should apply equally to the mother.

steps.title: The mother feels her own body
steps.stepSummary: A woman can sense whether the baby's head came out, so there is no doubt in her case.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman senses it in herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the mother would feel it if the baby's head came out. So the doubt that caused the decree does not exist for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree is based on uncertainty. The mother knows from her own body what happened, so there is nothing to worry about in her case. The midwife cannot know this from the inside.

keyTerms.meaning: In herself, in her own body

phrases.english: A woman senses it in herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה מַרְגֶּשֶׁת בְּעַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the mother from the midwife
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mother is just as unsure as the midwife.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mother feels what happens in her own body, so there is no doubt in her case.

steps.title: Then the mother should tell the midwife
steps.stepSummary: If the mother knows, she can tell the חיה, and then no decree is needed for the midwife either.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let her tell the midwife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If the mother knows whether the head came out, she can tell the midwife, and then there is no need for a decree at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 11 seems to remove the doubt for the midwife too. The midwife could simply ask the mother. So why did the חכמים need a decree?

phrases.english: But let her say it to the midwife!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֵימָא לַהּ לְחַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 11 to challenge the need for the decree.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the decree on the midwife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the mother knows, she can pass the information on, and the doubt disappears.

steps.title: The mother is too distracted
steps.stepSummary: During labor the mother is too caught up in pain to tell the midwife.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is distracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word. The mother is too busy with the pain of birth to warn the midwife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother knows the facts, but in practice she will not tell anyone. So the midwife is still left in doubt, and the decree stands for her alone.
steps.whatToRemember: The decree falls on the חיה and not the mother. The mother knows what is happening in her own body, but she is too distracted to tell the midwife.

phrases.english: She is distracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: טְרִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mother will tell the midwife, so there is no doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mother is too distracted to say anything, so the midwife stays in doubt.

steps.title: What exactly do the two תנאים hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks to see the source of the מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the view of רבי ישמעאל, and what is the view of רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the two opinions mentioned earlier in step 7. It asks where their disagreement comes from. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 mentioned that רבי ישמעאל holds the עובר is טהור by Torah law and רבי עקיבא disagrees. Now the גמרא wants the actual source for this.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וּמַאי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא?
phrases.english: What is Rabbi Yishmael, and what is Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: He means: which opinions of theirs were we talking about before?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וּמַאי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the decree back to the Torah-level מחלוקת mentioned in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source text of the מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא

steps.title: The ברייתא on ״על פני השדה״
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses ״על פני השדה״ to exclude a fetus in the womb. רבי עקיבא uses it to include the grave cover and the grave walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: ״And whoever touches on the face of the field״ excludes a fetus inside a woman, says רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says it includes the גולל and the דופק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא where both תנאים explain the same words, ״על פני השדה״. They use those words for completely different lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רבי ישמעאל, ״on the face of the field″ means the corpse must be out in the open, so a fetus hidden in its mother does not make one טמא. רבי עקיבא uses the same words to add the parts of a grave as sources of טומאה. That leaves him free to treat the fetus as טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: On the face of the field, out in the open
Grave wall that the cover rests on

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים read the same words. One uses them to take something out (the fetus), and the other uses them to bring something in (the grave cover and walls).

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע עַל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה״ –
phrases.english: As it was taught: “And whoever touches on the face of the field”
to exclude a fetus in a woman's womb,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
to include the grave cover and the grave wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע עַל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת is about how to read ״על פני השדה״: excluding the fetus (רבי ישמעאל) or including גולל ודופק (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל knows גולל ודופק from tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל does not need a פסוק for the grave cover and walls, because he has it as a received הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל knows about the grave cover and wall as a received tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quietly asks where רבי ישמעאל gets the טומאה of the grave cover and walls, and answers right away. He learned it as a tradition, not from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל used ״על פני השדה״ for the fetus, so he has no פסוק left for גולל ודופק. The גמרא explains he does not need one, because the rule came down to him as a tradition.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael, the grave cover and the grave wall —
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: where does he learn these from?

phrases.english: he learned it as a tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, גּוֹלֵל וְדוֹפֵק – הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills the gap left in רבי ישמעאל's view by the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי ישמעאל learns the טומאה of גולל ודופק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From a received tradition, not from a פסוק.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא learn that the fetus is impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי עקיבא's source that a dead fetus in the womb is טמא by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא: a fetus inside a woman is impure by Torah law. From where does he know this?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to רבי עקיבא. He used ״על פני השדה״ for the grave parts, so where does he get that the fetus is טמא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds the fetus is טמא מדאורייתא. He needs a positive source for that, since his reading of ״על פני השדה״ does not say anything about the fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva, a fetus in a woman's womb
is impure by Torah law — from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, עוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי אִשָּׁה טָמֵא מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא – מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 16, now asking about רבי עקיבא's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי עקיבא's Torah source for the טומאה of a fetus in the womb

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: ״במת בנפש״ means a dead fetus inside a living person
steps.stepSummary: ״A corpse within a נפש″ describes a dead fetus inside a living mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: the פסוק says ״one who touches a corpse within the life″. Which corpse is inside the life of a person? You must say it is a fetus in a woman's womb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא gives רבי עקיבא's source. He reads ״במת בנפש״ as ״a dead body inside a living person,″ which can only mean a fetus inside its mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״בנפש״ is read as ״inside a life.″ The only case of a dead body inside a living person is a dead fetus in the womb. So the Torah itself says touching it makes a person טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A corpse that is inside a living being
You must say, it must be

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said: the verse says:
“Whoever touches a corpse within the life,”
which is a corpse that is inside the life of a person?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר זֶה עוּבָּר שֶׁבִּמְעֵי אִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: You must say this is a fetus in a woman's womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, אָמַר קְרָא: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּמֵת בְּנֶפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא learns it from ״הנוגע במת בנפש״, read as a corpse inside a living person.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל uses that פסוק for a רביעית of blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל reads ״בנפש האדם″ as teaching that a רביעית of blood from a dead person is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל needs this פסוק for a רביעית of blood that comes from a dead person, teaching that it makes things impure. As it says: ״one who touches a corpse, the נפש of a person″. What is the נפש of a person that makes things impure? You must say it is a רביעית of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי ישמעאל does not learn the fetus from רבי עקיבא's פסוק. He uses the same words for a different lesson: a רביעית of blood from a dead person is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, ״נפש האדם″ means the life of the person, which is his blood. The amount is a רביעית. Since the פסוק is already used for this, it is not available to teach anything about the fetus.
steps.whatToRemember: Each תנא uses each פסוק for only one lesson. רבי ישמעאל uses ״על פני השדה״ to exclude the fetus and ״במת בנפש״ for a רביעית of blood, and he knows גולל ודופק from tradition. רבי עקיבא uses ״על פני השדה״ for גולל ודופק and ״במת בנפש״ to make the fetus טמא.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael needs this verse
for a quarter-log of blood that comes from a corpse,
that it makes things impure, as it is said:
“Whoever touches a corpse, the life of the person,”
which is the life of a person that makes things impure?
You must say this is a quarter-log of blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִרְבִיעִית דָּם הַבָּאָה מִן הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק that רבי עקיבא used in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי ישמעאל does with ״הנוגע במת בנפש״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses it to teach that a רביעית of blood from a dead person is טמא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא has a broader rule about blood from two corpses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא does not use ״בנפש האדם״ for a רביעית דם. He holds that even a רביעית coming from two dead people together is טמא באהל, and a ברייתא quotes him asking for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא follows his own view. He says that even a quarter-log of blood that comes from two dead people makes things impure in a tent. A ברייתא teaches this: רבי עקיבא asked, from where do we know that a quarter-log of blood from two dead people makes things impure in a tent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא does not learn the רביעית דם law the way רבי ישמעאל does. It brings a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא asks for the source of his own, bigger rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, רבי ישמעאל used ״בנפש האדם״ to teach that a רביעית דם from one dead person is טמא. רבי עקיבא goes further: blood from two different dead people can join to make up the רביעית. Since he has a פסוק for that bigger rule, the one-person case is already included.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning; consistent with his view elsewhere
Makes people and things under the same roof impure
From where do we know? A request for a source

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva follows his own reasoning,
phrases.notes: He means: this is why רבי עקיבא doesn't need ״בנפש האדם״ for the רביעית דם law the way רבי ישמעאל does.

phrases.english: for he says: even a quarter-log of blood
that comes from two corpses
imparts impurity in a tent,
as it is taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
From where do we know that a quarter-log of blood
that comes from two corpses
imparts impurity in a tent?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי עקיבא does not use ״בנפש האדם״ for the רביעית דם law that רבי ישמעאל learns from it in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא holds a broader rule, that a רביעית from two dead people is טמא, so the one-person case is already covered.

steps.title: The verse: two people, one measure
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns his rule from ״ועל כל נפשת מת לא יבא״. ״נפשת״ is plural, meaning two people. ״מת״ is singular, meaning one combined measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says, "He shall not come upon any people that are a corpse." This means two people, and one measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the פסוק that proves blood from two dead people joins together to make one רביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״נפשת״ is plural, so it speaks about two people, and blood is called נפש. ״מת״ is singular, so their blood together counts as one שיעור. That means two half-amounts join to make a full רביעית that is טמא באהל.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'souls of a corpse'; plural souls with a singular corpse
The set minimum amount needed for a halacha to apply

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל learns a רביעית from one dead person from ״בנפש האדם״. רבי עקיבא learns from ״נפשת מת״ that blood from even two dead people joins to make one רביעית, so he uses ״בנפש האדם״ for a fetus inside its mother.

phrases.english: As it is stated:
"He shall not come upon any people that are a corpse,"
two people, and one measure.
phrases.notes: ״נפשת״ is plural, so two people. ״מת״ is singular, so their blood makes up one amount together.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְעַל כׇּל נַפְשֹׁת מֵת לֹא יָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנין question asked in the ברייתא in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: A רביעית דם from two dead people is טמא באהל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 21:11, ״ועל כל נפשת מת לא יבא״, with plural ״נפשת″ and singular ״מת״.

steps.title: משנה: the fetus's foreleg cut off before or after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. A fetus pushes its foreleg out while its mother is giving birth. If the leg is cut off before the mother is slaughtered, the flesh is טהור. If it is cut off after, רבי מאיר says the flesh became impure by touching a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An animal is having trouble giving birth, and the fetus pushes out its foreleg. If someone cuts off the leg and only then slaughters the mother, the flesh is pure. If he slaughters the mother first and then cuts off the leg, the flesh has touched a נבלה. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a case of a fetus whose foreleg came outside the womb. רבי מאיר says the order matters: cutting the leg before the slaughter versus after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matters. If the leg is cut off before the slaughter, the flesh stays טהור. If it is cut off after the slaughter, רבי מאיר holds that the mother's שחיטה did not make the leg that was outside permitted, so it counts as a נבלה. The slaughtered flesh was touching it, so the flesh is מגע נבלה. The next step shows the חכמים disagree about the leg's status.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the start of a new משנה
Made impure by touching a נבלה, an animal or limb not properly slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: 'The flesh' here means the rest of the meat, meaning the mother and the fetus inside her. It does not mean the cut-off leg itself.

phrases.english: Mishnah
An animal having difficulty giving birth,
and the fetus put out its foreleg,
phrases.notes: Literally 'its hand'. For an animal, that means its front leg.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲתָכָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט אֶת אִמּוֹ –
phrases.english: and he cut it off, and afterward slaughtered its mother:
the flesh is pure.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט אֶת אִמּוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ חֲתָכָהּ –
phrases.english: If he slaughtered its mother and afterward cut it off:
the flesh has the impurity of contact with a carcass,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בְּהֵמָה הַמְקַשָּׁה לֵילֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous sugya ends and a new משנה begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cut before the slaughter: the flesh is טהור. Cut after the slaughter: according to רבי מאיר, the flesh is מגע נבלה.

steps.title: The חכמים: contact with a slaughtered טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. They say the cut-off leg is like a טרפה שחוטה, so the flesh only has the lighter status of touching a טרפה שחוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: the flesh has the status of touching a טרפה that was slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their side of the מחלוקת in the משנה. They say the leg counts as a slaughtered טרפה, not a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the mother's שחיטה works on the leg enough that it is not a נבלה. It is a טרפה שחוטה, which may not be eaten. By Torah law a טרפה שחוטה does not make things impure. The רבנן only treated it as impure for קדשים, so the flesh's impurity is much lighter than רבי מאיר's.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden animal or limb that was nonetheless slaughtered. It is not a נבלה, and by Torah law it does not make things impure.

steps.whyThisMatters: The מחלוקת is about whether the mother's שחיטה has any effect on a limb that came outside the womb. That question shapes the rest of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
it has the impurity of contact with a slaughtered tereifa,
phrases.notes: The leg is treated like a slaughtered טרפה. Touching it only matters for קדשים, by rabbinic rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מַגַּע טְרֵפָה שְׁחוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים's opinion, which argues with רבי מאיר's ruling in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the leg is cut after the slaughter, the flesh is מגע טרפה שחוטה, not מגע נבלה.
